title: Loadgen replay checklist and tolerance matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical checklist and a small tolerance matrix for replaying loadgen runs against the serving runtime. Goal: make small-batch throughput runs reproducible enough to debug regressions and attribute noise vs real performance delta. It lives as a companion to the load orchestration playbooks (see linked artifacts).

Context and motivation:
- Observed pain: flaky throughput deltas between nominally identical runs; hard to triage whether variance comes from client-side timing, network jitter, GPU thermal behaviour, or kernel scheduling.
- Practical aim: define a minimal set of steps and a quantitative "tolerance matrix" that tells us when to accept a run as equivalent vs when to start deeper forensics.

Checklist before you start a replay run (fast pass):
1) environment & binary hygiene:
   - Confirm exact binary (git sha + build tag). Record runtime image and commit in the run notes.
   - Ensure no active deployments sharing GPUs with test cluster. Use isolated node pool if available.

2) hardware state:
   - Verify GPU clocks: set persistence mode and fixed clock ceilings for profile runs.
   - Check GPU driver version and CUDA/cuDNN. Log nvml output.

3) system loads & thermal state:
   - If possible, reserve nodes and allow 5–10 minute idle cool-down.
   - Capture baseline thermal telemetry (GPU temp, host CPU temp).

4) telemetry gates:
   - Turn on kernel-level tracing (when available) and sample perf counters.
   - Make sure runtime tracing hooks are enabled at the same verbosity levels as the golden run.

5) client config & RNG hygiene:
   - Use seeded request payloads when the model deterministic path is desired. Save seed file.
   - Fix client-side concurrency and pacing parameters; avoid adaptive pacing for replay runs.

6) warmup protocol (recommended default):
   - Two-phase warmup: (a) primer sequence of 50 short requests to populate KV caches; (b) occupancy sweep of 5 minutes at 30%, 60%, then target occupancy.
   - Use deterministic spacing for primer (constant 50 qps) to minimize arrival jitter during kernel JIT paths.

7) run orchestration:
   - Run duration: prefer 10 minute plateau after warmup for steady-state metrics.
   - Collect full percentile distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999), throughput, QPS, and per-token times.

8) observability capture:
   - Save raw traces, CUDA prof output, and aggregated telemetry export. Tag all artifacts with run id and seed.

Minimal JSON-quality run metadata to capture for every replay (always include):
- run_id, git_sha, image_tag, node_pool_id, target_qps, concurrency, request_shape_id, seed_file_id, warmup_profile_id, start_time, end_time

Tolerance matrix (quick reference): when to accept run as "equivalent" vs "requires investigation"
- throughput (avg qps): within ±2% => acceptable; 2–5% => caution, re-run; >5% => investigate.
- p95 latency: within ±4% => acceptable; 4–10% => caution; >10% => investigate.
- p99 latency: within ±10% => acceptable only if throughput also within ±2%; otherwise investigate.
- GPU kernel time mean: within ±3% => acceptable; >3% => investigate kernel path changes.
- GPU util: within ±6 percentage points => acceptable.
- variance (coefficient of variation of p95 samples across windows): if CV > 0.12 => label run noisy and treat as non-deterministic.

Operational guidance on re-runs:
- If in caution band, run two additional independent replays (same seed/file) and compare aggregated medians. If both new runs agree with baseline, accept; otherwise escalate.
- If noisy (CV high), run longer plateaus (×2 duration) and capture more windows before concluding.

Warmup heuristics and why they matter (notes for engineers):
- Short primer sequences reduce first-token jitters and cold-cache effects. For KV cache heavy workloads, primer size matters more than primer QPS.
- Occupancy sweeps expose queuing effects and kernel selection changes at different batch sizes; include them in preflight to ensure runtime picks the intended execution path.
- Avoid adaptive client throttling during warmup — it masks the system's true steady-state entry point.

Common failure modes and quick mitigations:
- Large step change in p99 but throughput stable: suspect tail GC, host OS noise, or background cron jobs — check host-level tasklist and systemd timers.
- Throughput drop with similar latencies: look for tokenization or request-shape mismatch that changes average tokens per request.
- Regressions only in long runs: check thermal throttling and sustained power draw. Use longer warmup or forced thermal stabilization.

Forensics playbook when tolerance exceeded:
1) reproduce with a different (but identical spec) node pool to rule out hardware trobles.
2) run microbench kernels (single-layer profiling) to isolate which op increased time.
3) enable higher-fidelity traces around top-k slow requests identified by tail sampler.
4) compare kernel selection logs between runs — look for different GEMM path or quantization fallback.

Example canonical run sequence (copy-paste friendly):
- checkout commit: <git_sha>
- build image: ci/builds/<image_tag>
- provision nodes: node-pool test-stable-3xA100
- cool-down: wait 600s idle
- primer: 50 requests @ 50 qps constant spacing (seed-file-20250208.json)
- occupancy sweep: 5min @ 30% occupancy, 5min @ 60%, 10min @ 100% (target)
- plateau: 10min steady target qps
- capture: store traces, perf counters, and runtime logs with run id

Notes on automation and CI gating:
- We should gate only on the most stable metrics (avg throughput and p95 medians) and never on raw p99 in short runs.
- For CI smoke tests, use shorter primer and 3-minute plateau with higher tolerance thresholds.

Open questions / things to try next:
- Empirically validate tolerance bands across GPU generations — are current ±2% / ±4% thresholds conservative for H100 vs A10?
- Add an automated thermal-stabilization step in the harness (smart cooldown or active pre-burn).
- Explore using synthetic micro-bursts to accelerate kernel path determinism detection.

Run notes template (one-line per field for easy ingestion):
run_id:
git_sha:
image_tag:
node_pool:
seed_file:
target_qps:
plateau_duration_secs:
warmup_profile:
observability_bundle_url:
acceptance_decision:

Summary: this doc is intentionally prescriptive and lightweight — the goal is pragmatic repeatability rather than perfect elimination of noise. Use the tolerance matrix as an escalation heuristic and update it when we have more cross-gen data.

If you use this checklist for an investigation, add a short post-mortem to the run notes and ping #eng-serving-runtime so we can iterate on thresholds and automation.
